name: Into the Woods
address: 3501 S. Tamiami Trail Suite 1175, Sarasota, FL 34239
blurb: Sondheim and Lapine's fairy-tale mash-up is playing at Rise Above Performing Arts' new theater on South Tamiami Trail, next to Connors Steak & Seafood. Eight performances across two weekends: evenings at 7:30 and Sunday matinees at 2:30, with tickets running about $22 to $35. Familiar characters up front, a much deeper second act, and an easy night out for families with older kids.

name: Sarasota Art Colony Cultural Heritage Exhibit
venue: Arts Advocates Gallery, Crossings at Siesta Key
blurb: A free look at the artists who put Sarasota on the cultural map: a dozen works by Sarasota Art Colony painters William Hartman, Martha Hartman, Wilfred Berg and Eugene White, hung alongside the Arts Advocates permanent collection and its Florida Highwaymen holdings. The gallery sits inside the Crossings at Siesta Key and opens Saturdays from 2 to 4 PM. Worth an hour if you want the backstory behind the town's arts reputation.

name: Sarasota Farmers Market
address: Lemon Ave & Main St, Sarasota, FL 34236
blurb: Downtown Sarasota's Saturday-morning staple: fresh produce, flowers, baked goods, coffee and local makers spread along Lemon Avenue and Main Street. Free to browse and dog-friendly, and the single easiest way to see downtown at its liveliest. Go early to beat the August heat.

name: Siesta Key Drum Circle
blurb: Sarasota's most-photographed weekly ritual: drummers, dancers, hula hoopers and a few hundred onlookers gather on the quartz sand just south of the Siesta Beach pavilion as the sun drops into the Gulf. Free, no experience needed, and bringing your own drum is encouraged. Park early, because the lot fills well before sunset.
